identityTradability.exchangeName: Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. - Common Stock

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Power conversion is required infrastructure for higher-density compute, and current enterprise-data growth shows material exposure; evidence does not establish exclusive control.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: AI/server, communications, storage/computing, automotive and industrial exposures diversify demand, while Enterprise Data reached 38.8% of Q2 revenue and is increasingly important.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Power management remains necessary across architectures, but socket displacement, customer redesign, integration and competing suppliers can shift content and economics.

structural-causal.name: supplyChainResilience
structural-causal.basis: Management describes a diversified global supply chain, but semiconductor supplier capacity/yield dependence remains a structural constraint.

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI power bottleneck exposure
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Enterprise Data growth shows power-management content scaling with AI/server infrastructure.

adversarial-red-team.name: thesisQuality
adversarial-red-team.basis: Exceptional current growth supports the thesis, while concentration, architecture substitution and a high execution bar remain material falsifiers.

adversarial-red-team.name: governancePower
adversarial-red-team.basis: Reviewed Beta evidence does not establish a complete current governance assessment.

adversarial-red-team.name: supplyChainResilience
adversarial-red-team.basis: Diversification efforts are positive, but supplier capacity/yield dependence and committed wafer exposure remain real semiconductor-chain risks.

expectations-execution.name: Execution momentum
expectations-execution.basis: Record revenue, broad sequential end-market growth and higher next-quarter guide.

items.risk: Enterprise Data has become a much larger revenue share, increasing sensitivity to AI infrastructure cycles and customer concentration.
Rapid sequential growth and aggressive capacity expansion raise the execution bar.
AI infrastructure demand can remain strong while MPS captures less value if power architectures integrate functions differently, competitors win sockets, or customer ramps change.
Supplier capacity and yield constraints can become a successor bottleneck as MPS expands capacity goals beyond $6B.
Enterprise Data represented 38.8% of Q2 2026 revenue, increasing sensitivity to AI/server ordering patterns and major platform cycles.
Stock-based compensation and a higher diluted share count create shareholder dilution pressure even while earnings are growing rapidly.
Supplier capacity, wafer commitments, yield issues and customer cancellations can create inventory, margin or fulfillment stress during a demand transition.
AI TAM growth is not equivalent to durable MPS socket share, pricing power or content per system.
A newly announced foundry partnership does not by itself establish production volume, yield, economics, timing or customer-specific demand conversion.

Foundry diversification can reduce single-path supply risk while adding qualification, ramp and execution complexity; no benefit should be scored until Alpha source-addresses the economics and timing.
